messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Political behaviour and attitudes in Berlin during the 1950s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS Berlin 1950s political attitudes survey dataset West Berlin 1950
ICPSR Berlin 1950 1955 political attitudes public opinion survey data
ZACAT Berlin 1950er politische Einstellungen Umfrage Datensatz
action.query: GESIS Berlin 1950s political attitudes survey dataset West Berlin 1950

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"The Political Situation in West Berlin (March 1958) — GESIS ZA0591","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0591","justification":"Highly relevant dataset based on a March 1958 survey of 1,096 respondents in West Berlin. Examines political attitudes, economic expectations, East–West political orientation, confidence in Western powers, perceptions of Berlin's future, attitudes toward East Germany, and willingness to relocate. Particularly valuable for studying political behavior and public opinion during the Cold War and the period leading up to the Berlin Crisis of 1958–1961."},{"title":"Political Questions (December 1958) — GESIS ZA0455","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0455","justification":"Survey conducted in December 1958 among 1,892 respondents in West Germany, including West Berlin. Covers attitudes toward the Berlin Crisis, Soviet intentions, German reunification, nuclear armament, and the preferred responses of Western governments. Useful for examining political attitudes during the 1958 Berlin Crisis, although the sample is not limited to Berlin residents."},{"title":"Conditions in the GDR (September 1958) — GESIS ZA3322","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.3322","justification":"A September 1958 survey of East German visitors attending the Interbau exhibition in West Berlin. Investigates attitudes toward German reunification, the Socialist Unity Party (SED), economic conditions in East Germany, Soviet influence, and relations between church and state. Particularly useful for investigating East German political attitudes among people who traveled to West Berlin. The sample should not be treated as representative of all East Berlin or East German residents."},{"title":"Political Attitudes in Berlin (Cumulative Dataset: November 1960 – January 1963) — GESIS ZA3481","url_or_doi":"https://www.da-ra.de/dara/study/web_show?detail=true&lang=en&mdlang=de&res_id=4788&widget=&widgetclient=","justification":"A cumulative survey dataset covering political attitudes in West Berlin between November 1960 and January 1963. Includes party preferences, voting behavior, perceptions of the CDU and SPD, attitudes toward Willy Brandt, confidence in American policy, and fears of international conflict. Although collected just after the 1950s, it is particularly valuable for examining the continuation of political developments originating in the 1958 Berlin Crisis and comparing attitudes before and after the construction of the Berlin Wall."},{"title":"Political Attitudes in Berlin (January 1963) — GESIS ZA3480","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.3480","justification":"Survey of political attitudes in West Berlin in January 1963. Provides a useful comparison with late-1950s political opinion by examining Berlin's political environment following the Berlin Wall's construction. Best suited to longitudinal research investigating how Cold War tensions affected political preferences and public attitudes from the late 1950s into the early 1960s."},{"title":"Political and Economic Attitudes of the Population of Berlin (April–May 1966) — GESIS","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0727","justification":"Survey of West Berlin residents examining perceptions of Berlin's political future, attitudes toward the governments of France, Britain, the United States, and West Germany, political party preferences, and media consumption. Although conducted in 1966, it provides comparative evidence for researchers investigating the longer-term development of Berliners' political attitudes following the crises of the 1950s."},{"title":"Political and Economic Attitudes of the Population of Berlin (February–March 1967) — GESIS ZA0536","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.0536","justification":"Survey of 437 West Berlin respondents examining political participation, party preferences, voting intentions, satisfaction with political leaders, confidence in Western powers, and attachment to Berlin. Some respondents participated in a longitudinal panel. Useful for tracking the evolution of political attitudes established during the 1950s, although the observations themselves date from 1967."}]}
